body: ## Automated Issue from Infrastructure Logs  **Severity**: P1   **Source**: kubernetes   **Pod**: code-server-xyz   **Namespace**: default    ### Pod Status Pod CrashLoopBackOff Container: code-server Exit Code: 2 Last Restart: 45 seconds ago Restart Count: 12  ### Error Message FATAL: Cannot bind to port 8080: Address already in use  ### Root Causes 1. Port already bound (most likely)    - Another container/process using port 8080    - Stale connection not cleaned up after pod restart  2. Race condition during pod startup    - Multiple pods starting simultaneously  3. ConfigMap/volume mount issue    - Missing or corrupt port configuration  ### Troubleshooting 1. Check if port is actually bound:    kubectl exec -it code-server-xyz -- lsof -i :8080    kubectl exec -it code-server-xyz -- netstat -tlnp | grep 8080  2. Check node resources:    kubectl describe node <node-name>  3. Review pod events:    kubectl describe pod code-server-xyz  4. Check pod logs:    kubectl logs code-server-xyz --previous    kubectl logs code-server-xyz --tail=50  ### Fix Steps 1. Terminate existing code-server pods to free port 2. Increase readiness probe initial delay 3. Add port conflict detection to startup script 4. Redeploy pod  --- Action Required: Manual pod restart after fixing port conflict
title: [AUTO-TRIAGE] kubernetes: Pod CrashLoopBackOff - Port binding conflict on code-server

body: ## Automated Issue from Infrastructure Logs  **Severity**: P1   **Source**: syslog    ### Logged Events 1. kernel panic: attempting to kill init! 2. docker: container code-server exited with code 137 (OOMKilled) 3. auth: 5 failed login attempts from 203.0.113.42 in 30 seconds 4. postgresql: connection timeout after 30 seconds waiting for lock  ### Correlation Analysis Multiple infrastructure components failing suggests: - Likely Cause: Memory pressure on host (OOMKilled is strong signal) - Secondary: Database lock contention / slow queries - Security: Brute force attempt (5 failed logins in 30s)  ### Remediation Steps 1. Immediate: Check memory on host    free -h    top -b -n1 | head -20  2. Investigate kernel panic: journalctl -xb  3. Check PostgreSQL locks  4. Security: Review auth logs  5. Docker: Restart container    docker compose restart code-server  ### Long-term Actions - Increase host memory allocation - Add memory monitoring to Prometheus - Implement query optimization for slow queries - Add rate limiting to auth endpoints  --- Requires Human Investigation - Not Auto-Recoverable
title: [AUTO-TRIAGE] system: Multiple infrastructure errors - kernel panic, Docker OOMKilled, auth failures

body:
## Objective

Verify that infrastructure logs from all sources automatically create GitHub issues without manual intervention.

## Scope - All Log Sources
- [x] Terraform deployment logs (apply/plan failures)
- [x] HAProxy failover events (primary/replica transitions)
- [x] System logs (kernel panics, Docker crashes, auth failures)
- [x] Kubernetes pod lifecycle events (CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, etc.)
- [x] Container health check failures

## Implementation Status

### Γ£à Completed
- Error triage engine script (\scripts/error-triage-engine.sh\)
- Log collectors for all infrastructure sources (10 scripts in \scripts/observability/\)
- Loki log aggregation backend (config: \config/loki-config.yaml\)
- Promtail log shipping (config: \config/promtail-config.yaml\)
- GitHub issue bridge (\scripts/observability/log-to-github-bridge.sh\)
- IaC deployment scripts (idempotent, immutable)
- End-to-end test suite

### ΓÅ│ In Progress
- Deployment to production hosts (192.168.168.31 and .42)
- Verification that logs actually flow through the pipeline
- Testing that GitHub issues are created automatically

## Deployment Steps
1. Run pre-flight validation: \\\ ash scripts/validate-logging-pipeline-iac.sh\\\
2. Deploy to primary: \\\ ash scripts/deploy-logging-pipeline-iac.sh --host 192.168.168.31 --install\\\
3. Deploy to replica: \\\ ash scripts/deploy-logging-pipeline-iac.sh --host 192.168.168.42 --install\\\
4. Verify: \\\ ash scripts/observability/test-log-pipeline.sh --all\\\

## Acceptance Criteria

### Phase 1: Logs Flowing to Loki
- [ ] Loki is deployed and accessible on both hosts
- [ ] Promtail is shipping logs successfully
- [ ] All log sources appear in Loki query results
- [ ] Log retention policy is working (30-day retention)

### Phase 2: Error Pattern Detection
- [ ] Error-triage-engine detects recurring error patterns
- [ ] Clustering groups similar errors together
- [ ] False positive rate is acceptable (< 5%)

### Phase 3: GitHub Issue Creation
- [ ] New error patterns trigger GitHub issue creation within 5 minutes
- [ ] GitHub issues include proper context (logs, stack traces, severity)
- [ ] Duplicate errors update existing issues instead of creating new ones
- [ ] Issues are labeled appropriately (error-triage, P0/P1/P2, source-type)

### Phase 4: Production Verification
- [ ] Both production hosts are running the logging pipeline
- [ ] End-to-end test suite passes
- [ ] Real infrastructure events trigger GitHub issues automatically
- [ ] Issue creation meets SLA (< 5 minutes from event to issue)

## Related Issues
- #378 - P0 Automated Error Triage Framework
- #1069 - Infrastructure Observability
- #1194 - EPIC Observability

## Notes

All scripts are production-ready, tested, and committed to main. This issue tracks the deployment and live verification phase.

See \docs/observability/LOG-PIPELINE-TO-GITHUB-ISSUES.md\ for complete documentation.

---

**Status:** Ready for deployment  
**Effort:** ~4-6 hours (deployment + verification)  
**Owner:** @kushin77  
**Labels:** P0, observability, infrastructure, logging

body: ## Problem  Several infrastructure components lack comprehensive metrics and dashboards:  1. **Session-Broker Metrics** (missing)    - Session creation/destruction rate    - Active session count    - Container spawn/cleanup latency    - Error rates  2. **PostgreSQL Metrics** (partial)    - Connection pool saturation    - Query latency percentiles    - Replication lag (master/replica)    - Backup/restore job metrics  3. **Redis Metrics** (missing)    - Cache hit/miss rates    - Memory fragmentation    - Eviction rates (if any)    - Persistence (AOF) metrics  4. **Network/DNS Metrics** (missing)    - DNS resolution time    - Failover trigger events    - Cross-host latency  ## Solution  ### Phase 1: Add Exporters - [ ] Add postgres_exporter service to docker-compose.yml - [ ] Add redis_exporter service for Redis metrics - [ ] Add custom session-broker metrics endpoint - [ ] Add Caddy metrics endpoint  ### Phase 2: Prometheus Scrape Jobs - [ ] Add postgres_exporter scrape job (10 essential queries) - [ ] Add redis_exporter scrape job - [ ] Add session-broker /metrics endpoint - [ ] Add Caddy /metrics endpoint  ### Phase 3: Grafana Dashboards - [ ] PostgreSQL Performance Dashboard (connections, queries, replication) - [ ] Redis Health Dashboard (memory, eviction, persistence) - [ ] Session-Broker Dashboard (active sessions, spawn latency, errors) - [ ] Infrastructure Overview Dashboard (all key metrics)  ### Phase 4: Alerts - [ ] PostgreSQL replication lag > 10s - [ ] Redis memory > 80% usage - [ ] Session-broker error rate > 5% - [ ] Caddy HTTP error rate > 1%  ## Acceptance Criteria  - [ ] All 4 exporters running and scraping - [ ] Prometheus targets show 100% UP status - [ ] 4 Grafana dashboards created and populated - [ ] 4+ alerting rules configured - [ ] Documentation updated with metrics inventory  ## Estimated Effort  8-12 hours  ## Priority  P2 (enhances production visibility)  ## Related  - #954 (HA Epic - depends on observability) - #965 (Observability EPIC)
title: P2: Infrastructure Observability - Add Missing Metrics and Dashboards
